cases.name: Victoria Lynn Fowler Anderson
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Victoria graduated from Kingwood High School in 2007, then attended Lipscomb University in Nashville, Tennessee. She graduated cum laude from Lipscomb in 2011 with a bachelor’s degree in Finance and a minor in Mathematics, and received the College of Business Senior Award for Excellence in Economics/Finance. In 2016, she received her MBA from Texas A&M University. She worked for Hess Corporation, Energy XXI, and Insperity.

Growing up, Victoria loved traveling to visit family, going to church camp, and taking trips with her family and friends.

Victoria was very creative and loved all types of arts and crafts. She enjoyed baking and decorating cakes and cookies, and she was especially talented as a makeup artist. She played the piano and the alto saxophone. She also enjoyed decorating her home and watching Aggie football.

Victoria was married in 2016, and gave birth to her son, James Robert, in 2020. He was her greatest joy and the light of her life. Victoria loved her family dearly.

Above all, Victoria loved the Lord. In 2007, she was baptized into Christ, and she remained faithful for the rest of her life. Serving others was very important to her, and she enjoyed being surrounded by her church family."
cases.narrative: Victoria called 911 saying her husband was trying to kill her. Moments later, the 911 operator allegedly heard a gunshot. He reportedly refused to surrender, sparking a five-hour standoff with the SWAT team. Houston police officers discovered Victoria's body in the home. Their 3-year-old son was unhurt, but found covered in his mother's blood.
